note: All 50 items are single-best-answer MCQs on GI physiology -- gastric/pancreatic/biliary/salivary secretion, motility, hormonal control (gastrin, secretin, CCK, somatostatin), digestion and absorption physiology. That is lane HU-GIT-301-A's subject (Physiology), not this lane's. Reviewed all 50 stems against the four subjects this lane owns (Pathology, Pharmacology, Parasitology, Biochemistry): only Q40 names a drug (Omeprazole) and tests its mechanism/site of action, which belongs to Pharmacology by the 'drug and therapeutic-class labels belong to pharm' convention in 01-subjects-and-topics.md. Q2, Q4 and Q21 mention a drug class or a vitamin-deficiency mechanism in passing (H2-receptor antagonist as a distractor; cobalamin/fat-soluble-vitamin absorption) but the concept actually tested in each is GI motility/secretion regulation or absorption physiology, not a drug mechanism or a biochemical pathway, so they are left to lane A.
